title: Implement known-issues landing page + tagging system in redwood-docs; add cross-links from Support/CS references
creator: Elliot Price
project: CS & Support Escalation Playbook + Known-Issues Sprint (2026-02)
description:
Background
Support/CS is running a known-issues sprint to reduce repeat tickets and improve time-to-mitigation. We need a first-class landing page in redwood-docs that (a) lists known issues + workarounds, (b) supports consistent tagging (region/model/tier), (c) makes escalation guidance obvious, and (d) is easy for Support to link from Jira workflows and macros.

Problem
Today, workaround content is scattered across ad-hoc docs pages and not consistently discoverable. Support often pastes guidance manually and customers miss the most current workaround/escalation criteria.

Goals / success criteria
- Single landing page for Known issues & workarounds with filtering by tags.
- Standardized frontmatter schema so authors can publish new items without custom page wiring.
- Each issue page clearly includes: symptoms, impact, affected models/regions/tiers, workaround steps, and "When to escalate".
- Cross-links added from Support/CS internal references (so Support workflows reliably point to the hub).
- No customer-sensitive details on public pages.

Non-goals
- Rewriting the actual workaround article content (owned by Docs writers + reviewers).
- Building an incident/status-page system (handled via existing status page tooling).

Proposed IA (aligned with DES-233)
- New hub route: /support/known-issues (or /docs/support/known-issues depending on existing nav conventions; final path decided in PR).
- Landing page sections:
  1) "Top known issues" (recent + high-impact)
  2) Filters: Product tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), Region, Model family, Category (Streaming, Quotas, Autoscaling, Installer/Upgrades, Audit logs)
  3) Table/list of entries with: title, short summary, tags, last updated, workaround available (yes/no), and a prominent "Escalate if…" snippet.
  4) Callout: "If you’re experiencing a widespread outage, check Status" with link.

Tagging + metadata (frontmatter)
Implement a minimal schema in markdown frontmatter used by the landing page generator:
- slug (string)
- title (string)
- summary (string)
- product_tiers (comma-separated list: hosted|dedicated|private)
- regions (comma-separated list; allow "all")
- models (comma-separated list; allow "multiple")
- categories (comma-separated list)
- workaround_status (workaround|mitigated|fixed|investigating)
- last_updated (YYYY-MM-DD)
- escalation_criteria (string; short)

Implementation notes
- Update redwood-docs build to collect all known-issues pages from a single directory (e.g., /content/known-issues/*) and generate the landing page list from frontmatter at build time.
- Filtering:
  - Client-side filtering is acceptable initially (dataset small; <100 items).
  - Use URL query params for shareable filtered views (e.g., ?tier=dedicated&category=autoscaling).
- Make "When to escalate" a required section on article template; fail CI if missing (lightweight lint).
- Ensure entries are included in sitemap + searchable by docs search.

Cross-links to add (internal navigation + references)
- Link hub from Support/CS escalation playbook pages and known-issues index (Confluence will point to docs hub; docs hub should point back to escalation criteria where appropriate).
- Add links from SDK troubleshooting sections (streaming, 429) to relevant issues.
- Add a short link block in Support macros doc (separate ticket PM-914 covers macro formatting; this ticket ensures the hub URL is stable and easy to reference).

Acceptance criteria
- Landing page renders in production docs build and includes at least the initial sprint articles.
- Each known-issue article shows tags + last_updated + escalation guidance.
- Filters work and are linkable.
- CI/docs lint prevents publishing a known-issue page without escalation guidance.
- Navigation includes an obvious entry point (Support/Troubleshooting section).

Test plan
- Local: yarn dev + verify landing loads with expected items.
- Local: yarn build to confirm generator works in production build.
- Verify query param filtering + tag chips.
- Verify docs search indexing (at least titles/summary) includes known-issues pages.

Rollout
- Merge behind normal docs deploy; no feature flag.
- Post-merge: announce final hub URL to Support/CS to update macros and Jira automation pointers.

Risks / open questions
- Path/IA finalization: ensure we don’t break existing doc URLs; add redirects if necessary.
- Keep content customer-safe: hub should only include articles marked safe-for-public (implicit by directory location; no internal-only pages included).

References
- Design: DES-233 (Known-issues page layout)
- Product criteria: PM-913 (Known-issue publication criteria)
- Related docs PR expected to include content + template updates (see linked PR).
comments: 2026-02-05 — Elliot Price: Aligning on URL path with Docs/DevEx. Preference: /support/known-issues because Support will paste into tickets; shorter is better. Please confirm nav placement doesn’t conflict with existing /support section.

2026-02-06 — Benji Okafor: Implementing frontmatter collector + landing page list as part of the docs build. Keeping filters client-side for now; if search/scale needs it later we can move to precomputed indices.

2026-02-08 — Wei Chen: Please make "When to escalate" unavoidable—Support needs something copy/paste ready. Suggest a required callout component at top of each article (short) + full section later in page.
2026-02-10 — Kira Thompson: For Private/Dedicated issues, we should allow "models=multiple" and be explicit in the summary instead of trying to enumerate every SKU in tags.

2026-02-12 — Benji Okafor: Added lint check: known-issues pages must include an EscalationCriteria component (or section header). CI fails otherwise. Also added query param persistence so Support can send a filtered link to customers (e.g., Private + upgrades).

2026-02-14 — Elliot Price: Final review—ensure we don’t include any internal-only Confluence links on public pages. Keep escalation guidance phrased as "contact Support" vs naming internal teams/on-call.
2026-02-16 — Benji Okafor: Shipped with initial batch of articles and tags. Follow-up: we should add a small "Last reviewed" field later (separate ticket) so Support knows freshness beyond last edit.
